data.description:
The bridge emits 0, 1, 2, 3 (another pass in flight), 4 (phase gate blocked) and 75 (reschedule).
Collapse to 0/1/2, folding the benign states into 0 with an explanatory message.

**The current arrangement has a live bug that proves the point.** The only consumer in the repo,
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:265-270`, whitelists 0/75/3 — and OMITS 4. So a
deliberately paused bridge fails CI red every 20 minutes. A whitelist that must be re-audited every
time a code is added is the wrong shape; deleting it beats extending it.

A second, inconsistent copy of the policy exists: `_lib_ops.py:115` raises unless the code is in
`(0, 75)` — treating 75 as benign but NOT 3, so a library caller hitting the perfectly normal
in-flight case gets a `RebarError` while CI logs it as benign.

OSS validation supports the collapse. Of seven comparable tools, only three offer a distinct
"succeeded, nothing to do" code (rclone 9, `git diff --exit-code`, `terraform plan
-detailed-exitcode`) and ALL THREE are opt-in and off by default; the four backup/transfer tools
closest to a scheduled bridge do not offer one at all. rclone attaches an explicit warning to its
own flag: "turns a usually non-fatal error into a potentially fatal one".

The shape distinction: git/terraform/rclone flags serve INTERROGATIVE invocations where the exit
code is the return value. A scheduled bridge is IMPERATIVE — a supervisor asking whether it broke.
For that shape, non-zero means a human should look.

Objection considered and answered: folding benign into 0 does not lose the ability to alert on a
dead bridge, because an exit code is per-invocation and "nothing for a week" is cross-invocation.
`bridge status --max-age` asserts liveness deliberately rather than accidentally.

ONE PRECONDITION before deleting 75: verify nothing keys off it. 75 is `EX_TEMPFAIL` from
sysexits.h, and a systemd unit using `RestartForceExitStatus=75` would be a real consumer. Note
`pass_io.py:34`'s comment gives an unrelated rationale ("outside the range used by common POSIX
utilities"), so the sysexits agreement appears to be coincidence — but check the deployment units.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The bridge emits only 0, 1, 2
- [ ] Benign outcomes exit 0 with a one-line explanation naming the state
- [ ] The CI whitelist `case` block is deleted
- [ ] `_lib_ops.py`'s divergent policy is removed in the same change
- [ ] Deployment units are checked for a consumer of 75 before it is retired
- [ ] `docs/exit-codes.md` records the change (the contract is being unfrozen deliberately; no deprecation window)
data.title: Collapse bridge exit codes to 0/1/2 and move the policy into core
